name: weclapp Cloud ERP
description: Read and write weclapp Cloud ERP data: customers, suppliers, contacts and leads, quotations, sales orders, invoices, articles, stock, purchase orders, tasks and time records. Popular ERP for German SMBs.
instructions:
weclapp is a cloud ERP for small and mid-sized companies. This connector reads and writes weclapp through the REST API v2: parties (customers, suppliers, contact persons, leads), quotations, sales orders, sales invoices, articles and stock, purchase orders, tasks, comments and time records. Recurring invoices and opportunities are read-only.

**Getting credentials**
1. In weclapp, open your user menu → **My settings** → **API** and copy the API token into `WECLAPP_API_TOKEN`. Each user has one token; generating a new one invalidates the old one.
2. Set `WECLAPP_TENANT` to the first part of your weclapp address only: for `acme.weclapp.com`, enter `acme`. Requests go to `https://acme.weclapp.com/webapp/api/v2` with the token in the `AuthenticationToken` header.

**Permissions follow the user**: the token acts as the weclapp user it belongs to, so records that user's role cannot see are missing from the results. Use a user with read access to sales, CRM and articles, and write access to whatever the AI should change. A write the user's role does not allow answers 403.

**Finding records**: get tools take the internal id, a numeric string such as `"3346"`, not the document number. To find a document by its number, filter the list tool: `orderNumber-eq=SO-1042`, `invoiceNumber-eq=RE-1042`, `quotationNumber-eq=AN-1042`, `articleNumber-eq=A5101`. Customers and suppliers both live under `/party`: filter with `customer-eq=true` or `supplier-eq=true`.

**Filter syntax**: `filter` is sent as query parameters written `property-operator=value` and joined with `&`, e.g. `paymentStatus-eq=OPEN&dueDate-lt=1767225600000`. Operators: `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `gt`, `le`, `ge`, `like`, `ilike`, `in`, `notin`, `null`, `notnull`. `-null` and `-notnull` take an empty value (`customerNumber-notnull=`); `-in` takes a bracketed list. A property name that does not exist returns HTTP 400, in `filter` and in `properties` alike. Sales documents have no `customerName`: the name is in `recordAddress`, the link is `customerId`.

**Data formats**: dates are Unix epoch milliseconds, in responses and in filters (2026-01-01 00:00 UTC is `1767225600000`). Prices and quantities come back as decimal strings such as `"119.00"`. Unpaid invoices are `paymentStatus-eq=OPEN`, cancelled ones `status-eq=CANCELLED`, credit notes `salesInvoiceType-eq=CREDIT_NOTE`: leave credit notes out when adding up revenue.

**Pagination and limits**: `page` starts at 1; `pageSize` defaults to 100 and is capped at 1000. Fetch the next page until a page returns fewer rows than `pageSize`, and pass only the fields you need in `properties` on large lists. weclapp has no fixed rate limit, but it queues requests under heavy load and answers HTTP 429 after 30 seconds in the queue: wait, then retry.

**Recurring invoices**: `/recurringInvoice` is not part of weclapp's published OpenAPI file. If `weclapp_list_recurring_invoices` returns 404 on a tenant, the resource is not available there; invoices generated from a recurring invoice still carry its `recurringInvoiceId`.

**Writing to weclapp**: every write tool changes the live ERP. Read the record first, tell the user what will change, and wait for their confirmation. The delete tools are installed switched off. If a write tool named here is missing, the connector was set up before it existed: ask the user to apply the connector update in AnythingMCP.
- Partial updates: the `weclapp_edit_*` tools send `PUT` with `ignoreMissingProperties=true`, weclapp's documented way to change single fields, so fields you leave out keep their values. Send only what changes: read-only fields such as `createdDate`, `statusHistory` or amounts are refused with HTTP 400 ("property ... is read-only"), so never copy a whole record back.
- Lists are replaced, not merged: when you send `addresses`, `contacts`, `partyEmailAddresses`, `orderItems`, `quotationItems` or `articlePrices`, include every entry to keep by its `id` (the id alone keeps it unchanged) and new entries without an id. An entry you leave out is deleted.
- Optimistic locking: pass the record's `version` from your last read and weclapp refuses the change with HTTP 409 "optimistic lock error" if someone changed it meanwhile; read again and retry. Without `version` the check is skipped.
- `dryRun: true` on create, edit and delete tools makes weclapp validate the request and answer without saving.
- References are ids (`customerId`, `responsibleUserId`, `unitId`, `warehouseId`...). `weclapp_list_reference_data` lists users, warehouses, storage places, units, taxes, currencies, payment terms and the other lists those ids point to.
- Decimals are sent as strings (`"quantity": "2"`, `"unitPrice": "119.00"`) and dates as epoch milliseconds. A position with your own price needs `manualUnitPrice: true` next to `unitPrice`.
- Status changes: `weclapp_set_sales_order_status` sends the status alone (weclapp refuses a reopen combined with other changes), `weclapp_cancel_sales_order` cancels or closes an order, `weclapp_set_quotation_status` uses weclapp's quotation status action. `weclapp_invoice_sales_order` creates a draft invoice from an order; every call creates another one.
- Stock is changed by bookings (`weclapp_book_stock_in`, `weclapp_book_stock_out`), not by editing the article; they take effect at once.

**Cloud reachability**: `*.weclapp.com` is publicly reachable over HTTPS.

WECLAPP_TENANT.help: The first part of your weclapp address: acme for acme.weclapp.com. Not the whole address.

WECLAPP_API_TOKEN.label: API token
WECLAPP_API_TOKEN.help: In weclapp: your user menu → My settings → API → API token.

tools.name: weclapp_list_customers
tools.description: List parties (customers/suppliers/contacts) from weclapp ERP. In API v2 customers and suppliers are unified under /party: pass filter='customerNumber-notnull=' to restrict to customers, or filter='supplierNumber-notnull=' for suppliers (the -null/-notnull operators take an EMPTY value, NOT '=true'). Use `properties` to limit returned fields (e.g. 'id,customerNumber,company,firstName,lastName,email') to reduce payload size.

properties.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return, e.g. 'id,customerNumber,company,firstName,lastName,email'

filter.description: weclapp v2 filter expression. The property+operator IS the param name (no 'filter=' wrapper). Examples: 'partyType-eq=ORGANIZATION', 'customerNumber-notnull='. Note that the -null/-notnull operators take an EMPTY value, not '=true'.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending (e.g. '-createdDate')

tools.name: weclapp_get_customer
tools.description: Get a specific party (customer/supplier/contact) by ID. In API v2 this maps to /party/id/{id}.

tools.name: weclapp_list_sales_orders
tools.description: List sales orders from weclapp ERP. Returns order numbers, amounts, status and the record address. NOTE: salesOrder has NO 'customerName' field: do not request it in `properties` (weclapp returns 400). The customer's name is in `recordAddress`; the customer link is `customerId`. Use `properties` to limit fields and `filter` to narrow results (e.g. 'orderNumber-eq=SO-1042'). Date fields are Unix epoch milliseconds (e.g. 'orderDate-gt=1767225600000').

properties.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending

tools.name: weclapp_list_invoices
tools.description: List sales invoices from weclapp ERP. Returns invoice numbers, amounts, due dates, and payment status. NOTE: invoice has NO 'customerName' field: do not request it in `properties` (weclapp returns 400); the name is in `recordAddress`, the link is `customerId`. Other common 400 traps: line items are `salesInvoiceItems` (not `invoiceItems`); the invoice-type field/filter is `salesInvoiceType` (not `invoiceType`); there is no `currencyName` (currency is `recordCurrencyId`, amounts are `netAmount`/`grossAmount`/`netAmountInCompanyCurrency`); a cancelled invoice is `status-eq=CANCELLED`, not an invoiceType. Use `filter` for queries like 'paid-eq=false'. Date fields are Unix epoch milliseconds (e.g. 'invoiceDate-gt=1767225600000' for 2026-01-01).

properties.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return

filter.description: weclapp filter. The property+operator IS the param name, so pass it as `property-operator=value` (NOT a `filter=` wrapper). Operators: -eq -ne -gt -lt -ge -le -like -ilike -in -notin -null -notnull (the -null/-notnull operators take an EMPTY value, e.g. 'articleNumber-notnull='). The -in/-notin operators need a BRACKETED comma list: 'id-in=[6501,84566]', NOT 'id-in=6501,84566' (that returns 400 'invalid parameter value'). Examples: 'articleNumber-eq=A5101', 'productionArticle-eq=true', 'name-ilike=%hammer%'. Combine with '&'.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending

tools.name: weclapp_list_articles
tools.description: List articles (products) from weclapp ERP. Returns article numbers, names, and stock info. Use `filter` like 'articleNumber-eq=ABC123' for SKU lookups. NOTE on prices: an article has NO direct `salesPrice`/`purchasePrice`/`lastPurchasePrice`/`averagePurchasePrice`/`valuationPrice` property (those return 400 'unknown property'). Sales prices live in the `articlePrices` sub-entity and purchase prices in `supplySources` (note: `supplySources`, not `articleSupplySources`); request those names in `properties` to get the nested price objects.

properties.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return

filter.description: weclapp filter. The property+operator IS the param name, so pass it as `property-operator=value` (NOT a `filter=` wrapper). Operators: -eq -ne -gt -lt -ge -le -like -ilike -in -notin -null -notnull (the -null/-notnull operators take an EMPTY value, e.g. 'articleNumber-notnull='). The -in/-notin operators need a BRACKETED comma list: 'id-in=[6501,84566]', NOT 'id-in=6501,84566' (that returns 400 'invalid parameter value'). Examples: 'articleNumber-eq=A5101', 'productionArticle-eq=true', 'name-ilike=%hammer%'. Combine with '&'.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending

Returns interval, next run, amounts and status. NOTE: no 'customerName' field: the name is in `recordAddress`, the link is `customerId`. Date fields are Unix epoch milliseconds.

tools.name: weclapp_list_opportunities
tools.description: List sales opportunities (Verkaufschancen) from weclapp CRM. Returns name, stage/status, expected value and the linked customer. NOTE: the linked party is referenced by `customerId` / `contactId`, not a name field. Date fields are Unix epoch milliseconds.

tools.name: weclapp_list_reference_data
tools.description: Look up the records other weclapp records point to by id, to turn a name into the id a write tool needs: users (responsibleUserId, task assignees, time records), warehouses and storage places, units, tax rates, currencies, terms of payment, payment and shipment methods, carriers, customer categories, sectors, lead sources and ratings, sales stages, titles, departments and roles of contact persons, cost centers, article categories and task lists. Read-only. Example: resource=user with filter='lastName-ilike=%meier%' to find a user's id.

properties.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. 'id,firstName,lastName,email' for users or 'id,name' for most lists.

filter.description: weclapp filter as query parameters: `property-operator=value`, joined with `&` (NOT a `filter=` wrapper). Operators: -eq -ne -gt -lt -ge -le -like -ilike -in -notin -null -notnull; -null/-notnull take an EMPTY value, -in/-notin a bracketed list (`id-in=[1,2]`). Examples: 'name-ilike=%netto%', 'email-eq=anna@example.com'.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending

tools.name: weclapp_list_comments
tools.description: List the comments on one weclapp record (sales order, quotation, invoice, party, task, ticket...), newest first with sort='-createdDate'. Also shows how weclapp spells the entityName of a record type before you add a comment with weclapp_add_comment.

entityName.description: Record type in weclapp's API spelling, e.g. salesOrder, quotation, salesInvoice, party, task, opportunity, ticket.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending, e.g. '-createdDate'.

tools.name: weclapp_add_party
tools.description: Create a customer or supplier (a party) in weclapp. Set customer: true for a customer, supplier: true for a supplier (both is allowed). weclapp assigns the customer or supplier number from its number range when you leave it out. Returns the new party with its id. Search with weclapp_list_customers first so you do not create a duplicate, and confirm the details with the user before creating.

partyType.description: ORGANIZATION for a company (use company), PERSON for a private person (use firstName/lastName).

customer.description: true to make the party a customer.

supplier.description: true to make the party a supplier.

company2.description: Second company line, e.g. the legal entity of a branch.

responsibleUserId.description: User responsible for this party (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=user).

customerNumber.description: Customer number; leave out to let weclapp assign the next one.

supplierNumber.description: Supplier number; leave out to let weclapp assign the next one.

addresses.description: Addresses; mark the main one with primaryAddress: true. Every address needs countryCode.

countryCode.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. DE. Required for every address.

company.description: Company name on this address when it differs from the party's.

invoiceAddress.description: true to use it as the invoice address.

deliveryAddress.description: true to use it as the delivery address.

fields.description: Further party fields by their weclapp names, e.g. {"customerPaymentMethodId": "4711", "customerTermOfPaymentId": "4712", "customerCategoryId": "4713", "tags": ["Messe"]}.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_add_contact_person
tools.description: Create a contact person (a party of type PERSON) in weclapp. Returns the new person with its id. To attach the person to a company, call weclapp_edit_party on the company with fields {"contacts": [...]} listing the id of EVERY contact it already has plus the new one: weclapp replaces the list, so a contact you leave out is detached. Confirm the details with the user before creating.

responsibleUserId.description: User responsible for this party (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=user).

personCompany.description: Company name shown with the person.

fields.description: Further party fields by their weclapp names, e.g. {"titleId": "3200", "addresses": [...]}.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_add_lead
tools.description: Create a lead in weclapp: a party with a lead status that is not a customer yet. List leads with weclapp_list_customers and filter='lead-eq=true'. To convert a lead later, call weclapp_edit_party with fields {"customer": true, "leadStatus": "CONVERTED"}. Returns the new party with its id. Confirm the details with the user before creating.

partyType.description: ORGANIZATION for a company (use company), PERSON for a private person.

responsibleUserId.description: User responsible for this party (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=user).

leadSourceId.description: Where the lead came from (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=leadSource).

addresses.description: Addresses; mark the main one with primaryAddress: true. Every address needs countryCode.

countryCode.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. DE. Required for every address.

company.description: Company name on this address when it differs from the party's.

invoiceAddress.description: true to use it as the invoice address.

deliveryAddress.description: true to use it as the delivery address.

fields.description: Further party fields by their weclapp names, e.g. {"sectorId": "4100", "description": "Met at the fair"}.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_edit_party
tools.description: Change fields of a customer, supplier, contact person or lead; fields you do not send keep their values (weclapp partial update, ignoreMissingProperties=true). Returns the updated party. Read it first (weclapp_get_customer), tell the user what will change and wait for their confirmation. Send only fields you change: copying a whole record back fails, because read-only fields such as createdDate or statusHistory are refused. A list field (addresses, contacts, partyEmailAddresses, orderItems...) is replaced as a whole: send every entry to keep, existing ones by their `id` (the id alone keeps an entry unchanged), new ones without an id; an entry you leave out is deleted.

partyId.description: The weclapp party ID (numeric string), not the document number.

fields.description: Fields to change by their weclapp names, e.g. {"responsibleUserId": "3555"}, {"vatIdentificationNumber": "NL803234168B01"}, {"customerNonStandardTaxId": "3621"}, {"customer": true}, {"salesInvoiceEmailAddressesId": "9001"}.

version.description: The record's `version` from your last read. weclapp then refuses the change (409 optimistic lock error) if someone else changed the record in the meantime: read it again and retry. Leave it out to skip that check.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_add_quotation
tools.description: Create a sales quotation (Angebot) for a customer, with its positions in the same call. weclapp assigns the quotation number and fills addresses, currency and terms from the customer. Returns the new quotation with its id and amounts. Read the customer and articles first, and confirm customer, articles, quantities and prices with the user before creating.

quotationItems.description: Positions. To set your own price send unitPrice with manualUnitPrice: true; otherwise weclapp prices the article for the customer.

articleId.description: Article ID (weclapp_list_articles). Leave out for a free text line with itemType FREE_TEXT.

quantity.description: Quantity as a decimal string, e.g. "2" or "1.5".

unitPrice.description: Net unit price as a decimal string, e.g. "119.00". Send it together with manualUnitPrice: true; without it weclapp uses the article's price.

manualUnitPrice.description: true when unitPrice is your own price rather than the article's price.

discountPercentage.description: Line discount in percent as a decimal string, e.g. "10".

title.description: Line title; defaults to the article name.

itemType.description: Line type; DEFAULT for an article line.

unitId.description: Unit ID when it differs from the article's unit.

taxId.description: Tax rate ID when it differs from the default.

unitCost.description: Purchase cost per unit as a decimal string; send manualUnitCost: true with it.

manualUnitCost.description: true when unitCost is your own value.

invoicingType.description: For a line whose article is a SERVICE: FIXED_PRICE or EFFORT (by time booked). weclapp may require it on service articles.

quotationDate.description: Quotation date; defaults to today. Unix epoch milliseconds.

opportunityId.description: Opportunity to link the quotation to.

fields.description:
Further quotation fields by their weclapp names, e.g. {"termOfPaymentId": "4712", "headerDiscount": "5", "recordOpening": "

Dear ...

"}.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_edit_sales_order

Find the id with weclapp_list_sales_orders, tell the user what will change and wait for their confirmation. Send only fields you change: copying a whole record back fails, because read-only fields such as createdDate or statusHistory are refused. A list field (addresses, contacts, partyEmailAddresses, orderItems...) is replaced as a whole: send every entry to keep, existing ones by their `id` (the id alone keeps an entry unchanged), new ones without an id; an entry you leave out is deleted.

salesOrderId.description: The weclapp sales order ID (numeric string), not the document number.

fields.description: Fields to change by their weclapp names, e.g. {"responsibleUserId": "3555"}, {"plannedDeliveryDate": 1767225600000}, {"orderNumberAtCustomer": "PO-778"}.

tools.name: weclapp_set_sales_order_status
tools.description: Set the status of a sales order: ORDER_CONFIRMATION_PRINTED marks it as confirmed, ORDER_ENTRY_IN_PROGRESS reopens it for changes. weclapp only accepts transitions its workflow allows and answers 400 otherwise; to cancel or close an order use weclapp_cancel_sales_order. Sends the status alone, as weclapp requires for a reopen. Returns the order. Confirm the change with the user first.

salesOrderId.description: The weclapp sales order ID (numeric string), not the document number.

version.description: The record's `version` from your last read. weclapp then refuses the change (409 optimistic lock error) if someone else changed the record in the meantime: read it again and retry. Leave it out to skip that check.

tools.name: weclapp_cancel_sales_order
tools.description: Cancel a sales order, or close it manually when parts of it were already shipped or invoiced (weclapp's cancelOrManuallyClose action). This ends the order and cannot simply be undone. Returns the order with its new status. Read the order first, tell the user exactly which order will be cancelled and wait for their explicit confirmation.

salesOrderId.description: The weclapp sales order ID (numeric string), not the document number.

tools.name: weclapp_invoice_sales_order
tools.description: Create a sales invoice from a sales order (weclapp's createSalesInvoice action), optionally combining further orders of the same customer into one invoice. The invoice is created as a draft with the open positions of the order(s); weclapp does not send it. Returns the new invoice under `result`. Every call creates another invoice, so first check the order's `invoiced` flag (weclapp_list_sales_orders with filter 'id-eq=<id>') and confirm with the user before invoicing.

salesOrderId.description: The weclapp sales order ID (numeric string), not the document number.

additionalSalesOrderIds.description: IDs of further sales orders of the same customer to put on the same invoice.

tools.name: weclapp_edit_sales_invoice
tools.description: Change fields of a sales invoice; fields you do not send keep their values (weclapp partial update), e.g. set the responsible user or the due date of a draft. weclapp refuses most changes to an invoice that is already booked or sent. Returns the updated invoice. Find the id with weclapp_list_invoices, tell the user what will change and wait for their confirmation. Send only fields you change: copying a whole record back fails, because read-only fields such as createdDate or statusHistory are refused. A list field (addresses, contacts, partyEmailAddresses, orderItems...) is replaced as a whole: send every entry to keep, existing ones by their `id` (the id alone keeps an entry unchanged), new ones without an id; an entry you leave out is deleted.

salesInvoiceId.description: The weclapp sales invoice ID (numeric string), not the document number.

fields.description:
Fields to change by their weclapp names, e.g. {"responsibleUserId": "3555"} or {"recordComment": "

...

"}.

version.description: The record's `version` from your last read. weclapp then refuses the change (409 optimistic lock error) if someone else changed the record in the meantime: read it again and retry. Leave it out to skip that check.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_add_task
tools.description: Create a task (Aufgabe) in weclapp, optionally assigned to users and linked to a customer or a record such as a sales order. Returns the new task with its id. Confirm subject, assignees and dates with the user before creating.

taskStatus.description: Status; NOT_STARTED for a new task.

customerId.description: Customer party the task is about.

entityReferences.description: Records the task belongs to, e.g. [{"entityName": "salesOrder", "entityId": "4400"}].

entityName.description: Record type, e.g. salesOrder, quotation, party.

fields.description: Further task fields by their weclapp names, e.g. {"taskVisibilityType": "PRIVATE", "taskLists": [{"id": "88"}]}.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_edit_task
tools.description: Change fields of a task; fields you do not send keep their values (weclapp partial update), e.g. mark it done with {"taskStatus": "COMPLETED"} or move the due date. Returns the updated task. Confirm the change with the user first. Send only fields you change: copying a whole record back fails, because read-only fields such as createdDate or statusHistory are refused. A list field (addresses, contacts, partyEmailAddresses, orderItems...) is replaced as a whole: send every entry to keep, existing ones by their `id` (the id alone keeps an entry unchanged), new ones without an id; an entry you leave out is deleted.

taskId.description: The weclapp task ID (numeric string), not the document number.

fields.description: Fields to change by their weclapp names, e.g. {"taskStatus": "COMPLETED"}, {"dateTo": 1767225600000}, {"assignees": [{"id": "91"}, {"userId": "3555"}]}.

version.description: The record's `version` from your last read. weclapp then refuses the change (409 optimistic lock error) if someone else changed the record in the meantime: read it again and retry. Leave it out to skip that check.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_add_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a weclapp record (sales order, quotation, sales invoice, party, task, ticket...). It appears in the record's comment stream, visible to colleagues; it is not sent to the customer unless publicComment is true. Returns the new comment. Confirm the text with the user before posting.

entityName.description: Record type in weclapp's API spelling, e.g. salesOrder, quotation, salesInvoice, party, task, opportunity, ticket. weclapp_list_comments on a record that already has comments shows the spelling.

htmlComment.description: The same comment as HTML, when it needs formatting.

privateComment.description: true makes it visible to you only.

publicComment.description: true makes it visible outside the company, e.g. on a ticket in the customer portal.

solution.description: true marks it as the solution of a ticket.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_add_time_record
tools.description: Book working time (Zeiterfassung) for a user in weclapp, optionally on a customer, a sales order, a task or a ticket. Durations are in seconds (1.5 hours = 5400). Returns the new time record. Confirm user, date, duration and what it is booked on with the user before booking.

userId.description: User the time belongs to (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=user).

startDate.description: When the work started. Unix epoch milliseconds.

billableDurationSeconds.description: Billable part in seconds; usually the same as durationSeconds, 0 for non-billable work.

customerId.description: Customer party the time is for.

articleId.description: Service article that prices the time.

hourlyRate.description: Hourly rate as a decimal string, when it differs from the article's.

fields.description: Further time record fields by their weclapp names, e.g. {"placeOfServiceId": "12", "printOnPerformanceRecord": false}.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_add_article
tools.description: Create an article (product or service) in weclapp, optionally with its sales prices. Returns the new article with its id. Search with weclapp_list_articles first (filter 'articleNumber-eq=...') so you do not create a duplicate, and confirm number, name, type, unit and prices with the user before creating.

articleNumber.description: Article number, unique in the tenant.

articleType.description: STORABLE for stocked goods, BASIC for goods without stock keeping, SERVICE for work and fees, SALES_BILL_OF_MATERIAL for a set, SHIPPING_COST for freight.

unitId.description: Unit ID, e.g. piece or hour (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=unit).

taxRateType.description: VAT rate type; STANDARD is the full rate (19% in Germany), REDUCED the reduced one.

id.description: ID of an existing price; leave out for a new price.

price.description: Price as a decimal string, e.g. "159.99".

currencyId.description: Currency ID (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=currency). Needed for a new price.

salesChannel.description: Sales channel, e.g. NET1 (net list price) or GROSS1. Needed for a new price.

priceScaleType.description: Scale type; SCALE_FROM with priceScaleValue "0" for a plain price.

priceScaleValue.description: Quantity the scale starts (or ends) at, as a decimal string, e.g. "0".

startDate.description: First day the price applies. Unix epoch milliseconds.

endDate.description: Last day the price applies. Unix epoch milliseconds.

customerId.description: Customer party ID for a customer-specific price.

availableInSale.description: true to offer it in sales documents.

fields.description: Further article fields by their weclapp names, e.g. {"manufacturerId": "812", "minimumStockQuantity": "10", "countryOfOriginCode": "DE"}.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_edit_article
tools.description: Change fields of an article (product); fields you do not send keep their values (weclapp partial update), e.g. name, EAN, manufacturer part number, minimum stock or whether it is sold. For sales prices use weclapp_set_article_prices; stock changes go through weclapp_book_stock_in and weclapp_book_stock_out, not through the article. Returns the updated article. Read it first (weclapp_get_article), tell the user what will change and wait for their confirmation. Send only fields you change: copying a whole record back fails, because read-only fields such as createdDate or statusHistory are refused. A list field (addresses, contacts, partyEmailAddresses, orderItems...) is replaced as a whole: send every entry to keep, existing ones by their `id` (the id alone keeps an entry unchanged), new ones without an id; an entry you leave out is deleted.

articleId.description: The weclapp article ID (numeric string), not the document number.

fields.description: Fields to change by their weclapp names, e.g. {"name": "Hammer 500 g"}, {"ean": "4006381333931"}, {"minimumStockQuantity": "20"}, {"active": false}, or the production bill of materials {"productionBillOfMaterialItems": [...]} (the whole list).

version.description: The record's `version` from your last read. weclapp then refuses the change (409 optimistic lock error) if someone else changed the record in the meantime: read it again and retry. Leave it out to skip that check.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_set_article_prices
tools.description: Change the sales prices of an article. weclapp keeps them as one list (articlePrices) and replaces it as a whole, so read the article first with properties='id,version,articlePrices' and send EVERY price that should remain: an existing price by its id (the id alone keeps it unchanged, id plus price changes it), a new price without an id; a price you leave out is deleted. Returns the updated article. Show the user the old and new prices and wait for their confirmation.

articleId.description: The weclapp article ID (numeric string), not the document number.

articlePrices.description: The complete list of sales prices after the change.

id.description: ID of an existing price; leave out for a new price.

price.description: Price as a decimal string, e.g. "159.99".

currencyId.description: Currency ID (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=currency). Needed for a new price.

salesChannel.description: Sales channel, e.g. NET1 (net list price) or GROSS1. Needed for a new price.

priceScaleType.description: Scale type; SCALE_FROM with priceScaleValue "0" for a plain price.

priceScaleValue.description: Quantity the scale starts (or ends) at, as a decimal string, e.g. "0".

startDate.description: First day the price applies. Unix epoch milliseconds.

endDate.description: Last day the price applies. Unix epoch milliseconds.

customerId.description: Customer party ID for a customer-specific price.

version.description: The record's `version` from your last read. weclapp then refuses the change (409 optimistic lock error) if someone else changed the record in the meantime: read it again and retry. Leave it out to skip that check.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_book_stock_in
tools.description: Book stock into a storage place (weclapp's bookIncomingMovement), e.g. goods received without a purchase order or an upward inventory correction. Takes effect at once and has no dry run; a wrong booking is corrected with weclapp_book_stock_out. Returns the stock movement. Confirm article, quantity and storage place with the user before booking.

quantity.description: Quantity as a decimal string, e.g. "80".

movementNote.description: Booking note, e.g. the reason for the correction.

batchNumber.description: Batch number, for articles managed in batches.

serialNumbers.description: Serial numbers, for articles with serial numbers (one per unit).

targetStoragePlaceId.description: Storage place to book into (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=storagePlace); defaults to the standard place.

batchNumberExpirationDate.description: Expiry date of the batch. Unix epoch milliseconds.

articleValuationPrice.description: Valuation price per unit as a decimal string.

tools.name: weclapp_book_stock_out
tools.description: Book stock out of a storage place (weclapp's bookOutgoingMovement), e.g. breakage, own use or a downward inventory correction. Takes effect at once and has no dry run; a wrong booking is corrected with weclapp_book_stock_in. Returns the stock movement. Confirm article, quantity and storage place with the user before booking.

quantity.description: Quantity as a decimal string, e.g. "80".

movementNote.description: Booking note, e.g. the reason for the correction.

batchNumber.description: Batch number, for articles managed in batches.

serialNumbers.description: Serial numbers, for articles with serial numbers (one per unit).

sourceStoragePlaceId.description: Storage place to book out of (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=storagePlace).

tools.name: weclapp_add_purchase_order
tools.description: Create a purchase order (Bestellung) to a supplier, with its positions in the same call. weclapp assigns the number and takes the supplier's terms; the order is not sent to the supplier. Returns the new purchase order with its id. Confirm supplier, articles, quantities, prices and delivery date with the user before creating.

purchaseOrderItems.description: Positions. unitPrice is the purchase price; without it weclapp uses the article's supply source price.

articleId.description: Article ID (weclapp_list_articles). Leave out for a free text line with itemType FREE_TEXT.

quantity.description: Quantity as a decimal string, e.g. "2" or "1.5".

unitPrice.description: Net unit price as a decimal string, e.g. "119.00". Send it together with manualUnitPrice: true; without it weclapp uses the article's price.

manualUnitPrice.description: true when unitPrice is your own price rather than the article's price.

discountPercentage.description: Line discount in percent as a decimal string, e.g. "10".

title.description: Line title; defaults to the article name.

itemType.description: Line type; DEFAULT for an article line.

unitId.description: Unit ID when it differs from the article's unit.

taxId.description: Tax rate ID when it differs from the default.

plannedDeliveryDate.description: Planned delivery date of this line. Unix epoch milliseconds.

warehouseId.description: Receiving warehouse (weclapp_list_reference_data resource=warehouse). weclapp needs one; leave out only if the tenant has a default.

orderDate.description: Order date; defaults to today. Unix epoch milliseconds.

plannedDeliveryDate.description: Planned delivery date. Unix epoch milliseconds.

salesOrderId.description: Sales order this purchase is for.

fields.description: Further purchase order fields by their weclapp names, e.g. {"note": "...", "termOfPaymentId": "4712", "externalPurchaseOrderNumber": "..."}.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_delete_party
tools.description: Delete a customer, supplier, contact person or lead. weclapp refuses when documents still refer to the party; block or deactivate it with weclapp_edit_party instead. Installed switched off: turn it on only if the AI should delete in weclapp, and confirm every deletion with the user.

partyId.description: The weclapp party ID (numeric string), not the document number.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

quotationId.description: The weclapp quotation ID (numeric string), not the document number.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

salesOrderId.description: The weclapp sales order ID (numeric string), not the document number.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_delete_task
tools.description: Delete a task. To keep it, set taskStatus COMPLETED or DEFERRED with weclapp_edit_task instead. Installed switched off: turn it on only if the AI should delete in weclapp, and confirm every deletion with the user.

taskId.description: The weclapp task ID (numeric string), not the document number.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_delete_comment
tools.description: Delete a comment from a record. Installed switched off: turn it on only if the AI should delete in weclapp, and confirm every deletion with the user.

commentId.description: The weclapp comment ID (numeric string), not the document number.

dryRun.description: true makes weclapp check the request and answer as if it had saved it, without saving anything. Use it to test an unusual or large write first.

tools.name: weclapp_delete_time_record
tools.description: Delete a time record. weclapp refuses once the time is invoiced. Installed switched off: turn it on only if the AI should delete in weclapp, and confirm every deletion with the user.

timeRecordId.description: The weclapp time record ID (numeric string), not the document number.
